Definition: {concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always}
BiblicalUsage: In the Old Testament, ʻêylôwm is the word for time out of mind, eternity. It appears in 2 Chronicles, and each time it carries that same plain sense.
TheologicalSignificance: This word, ʻêylôwm, does its job quietly — time out of mind, eternity — and I leave it at that.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
